title: Accounting and closing records, 1960-1965
summary: Financial papers for MKULTRA Subproject 119: invoice and ledger cards, review sheets, the fund's income and expense statements, obligation and invoice memos, receipts and vouchers for the $6,370 grant, and a 1965 request to close the account.

nodes.title: Invoice check list
nodes.summary: MKULTRA subproject card: original authorization 17 August 1960 on Allotment 1525-1009-1902 for $6,370.00, and invoice 1 in September 1960 for $6,370.00, leaving a zero balance.

nodes.title: Project status report
nodes.summary: Form from TSS/CD to TSS/OC: purpose is a critical review of the literature and scientific development on interpreting bioelectric signals from the human organism and activating human behavior by remote means. Date of obligation and expiration date N/A; progress satisfactory; project monitor redacted.

nodes.title: Sub-project no. 119 review sheet
nodes.summary: Review sheet: the researcher was to critically review literature on recording, analyzing and interpreting bioelectric signals and activating human behavior by remote means. Work ran September 1960 to July 1961 for about $6,370, was not classified, named no other sponsors, and was monitored by Gottlieb. Researcher and university were unwitting; probably nothing controversial.

nodes.title: Handwritten note on payments, 3 May 1965
nodes.summary: Note listing $3,500 and $850 sent for 1961-62 and $3,000 for 1962-63, with a slip dated 3 May 1965: 'we sent him the 3000 in reserve and that is it!'

nodes.title: Grant funds, income and expense, 1959-1963
nodes.summary: Statement for 2 October 1959 to 31 March 1963, certified as reported to the fund: $9,870 in grant funds, spending on salaries, research assistants, typists, the 1961 Bioelectronics Directory and abstracts, and income from book sales. Expense exceeded grant funds by $1,050.72 by August 1961; the final net excess was $86.41.

nodes.title: Analysis of income and expense, 1959-1965
nodes.summary: Table for 2 October 1959 to 16 March 1965: total expense $20,239.43, including $14,125.27 for personnel and $3,253 for printing the Bioelectronics Directory and abstracts, against $10,720 in grant funds and $5,908.32 from book sales, leaving expense $3,611.11 above funds.

nodes.title: Handwritten accounting notes
nodes.summary: Notes that the ULTRA grant of $6,370 was received by HEF on 29 September 1960, with accounting from 2 October 1959 to 25 July 1961 and entries of $2,470, $2,000 and $3,500 for October 1960, June 1961 and July 1961. A second note says project 134 accounted for a $22,000 grant for 1961-62.

nodes.title: Project summary card
nodes.summary: Card: purpose a critical review of literature and scientific developments on recording, analyzing and interpreting bioelectric signals from the human organism (MKULTRA 119); initiated September 1960; contractor redacted; cost $6,370; research completed and now being printed.

nodes.title: Memorandum on the Sub-project 119 account, 2 November 1965
nodes.summary: The balance in the MKULTRA Sub-project 119 memorandum account (760.0) appears to be in error, and missing papers block a full analysis. Program records show the research is completed and the final accounting received, so the account should be reviewed and closed if appropriate.

nodes.title: Obligation ledger sheet
nodes.summary: Ledger sheet showing $6,370 obligated for MKULTRA Sub 119 on 12 September 1960 and liquidated the same month by Invoice #1.

nodes.title: Memorandum for the Comptroller, 17 August 1960
nodes.summary: Chief, TSD/Research Branch tells the Finance Division that, under the 13 April 1953 authority from the DCI, Subproject 119 is approved and $6,370 of MKULTRA funds is obligated, charged to Allotment 1525-1009-1902.

nodes.title: Invoice no. 1, 12 September 1960
nodes.summary: Sidney Gottlieb, Deputy Chief, TSD/Research Branch, sends the Finance Division Invoice No. 1: a $6,370 cashier's check to reach the branch by 26 September 1960. It is a final invoice, but more funds are expected, so the files should stay open. A receipt for the check is attached.

nodes.title: Confidential funds posting voucher
nodes.summary: Confidential funds posting voucher for the $6,370 payment under MKULTRA Subproject 119. Names are redacted.

nodes.title: Accounting by individual for advance
nodes.summary: Form accounting for MKULTRA Sub 119 for 2 October 1959 to 31 March 1963: $6,370 received and $6,370 accounted for, with expenses shown on an attached certification. The back of the form carries printed instructions.

nodes.title: Note on finances, 6 May 1963
nodes.summary: Note enclosing the accounting for the special $6,370 grant and $3,500 of last year's grant money, which shows a deficit and omits April 1963 printing and advertising costs, plus an interim statement showing a $2,537.79 balance. A full-time technician will work on the project that summer.

nodes.title: Receipt for $6,370 check
nodes.summary: Receipt for a check dated 21 September 1960 for $6,370.00, signed by a redacted person on 29 September 1960.

nodes.title: Invoice and certifications
nodes.summary: Invoice No. 1 for services, $6,370.00, with certifications for the Deputy Chief, TSD/Research Branch and the Research Director that Subproject 119 is performing satisfactorily under the 13 April 1953 authority.

nodes.title: Memorandum for the Comptroller, 17 August 1960, second copy
nodes.summary: Second copy of the memo obligating $6,370 of MKULTRA funds for Subproject 119, charged to Allotment 1525-1009-1902, sent by TSD/Research Branch.

title: Project approval papers, 1960
summary: Memos and the proposal by which a consultant's bioelectric literature survey became MKULTRA Subproject 119 in 1960.

nodes.title: Draft memorandum for the record, 17 August 1960
nodes.summary: Draft memo setting up MKULTRA Subproject 119, with the attached project proposal and budget.

nodes.title: Purpose, cost and handling
nodes.summary: Subproject 119 funds a redacted researcher's critical review of literature on bioelectric signals and remote activation of human behavior, begun as consulting. It covers five areas, costs $6,370 including a $2,500 consulting fee, runs a year from 1 July 1960 as a grant-in-aid, and those involved are unwitting of the sponsor. Approved for obligation in September 1960.

nodes.title: Project proposal
nodes.summary: Proposal for a critical review of research on recording, analyzing and interpreting bioelectric signals and activating human behavior by remote means, starting with a survey across neurophysiology, biophysics, psychology and electronics in five areas. A list of laboratories, investigators and resources for the Bioelectronic study is in preparation.

nodes.title: Proposed budget
nodes.summary: Budget: $1,900 forwarded from September 1959 to February 1960, to be accounted for later, and $4,470 for 1 May to 31 December 1960 ($3,350 honoraria and salaries, $820 equipment and supplies, $300 travel), for a total of $6,370.

nodes.title: Memorandum for the record, 3 August 1960
nodes.summary: Gottlieb and others approved making a redacted researcher's consulting work a project: $6,370, including $2,500 already allotted, paid through a cover mechanism, the researcher unwitting of the sponsor. Points to convey: the project has an end point, a deadline probably in March 1961, and funds cover writing and publication.

nodes.title: Memorandum formalizing a proposal, 24 May 1960
nodes.summary: Work on an annotated bibliography and interpretive survey of psychophysiology research is going well. The first estimate was $2,500; the final cost will be about $6,370. The writer suggests a separately funded research task, promises a list of laboratories by late June, and asks that it start before 1 July.

title: Correspondence, July 1959 to February 1960
summary: Letters between a redacted grant-giving body and researchers about a survey of bioelectric research, EEG analyzers and other proposals, with checks and progress reports. Names and institutions are redacted.

nodes.title: Letter, 25 February 1960
nodes.summary: The writer found his meeting with a redacted group interesting and expects them to work in this area, especially analysis. He encloses a $1,000 check, asks whether the original $3,500 estimate will do, suggests formalizing the work as a project, and encloses a 'Report of the Special Committee'.

nodes.title: Letter, 24 December 1959
nodes.summary: Reply praising the researcher's progress report. A visit found little relevant work: continuous blood pressure recording, flicker fusion work and a portable jet-ink recorder. The writer encloses another $500 and accepts letting a redacted body hold expense receipts, but wants a statement at the project's end.

nodes.title: Progress report, 22 December 1959
nodes.summary: The researcher divides the bioelectronic study into four phases: organ systems generating electric potentials, recording, analysis and behavioral correlates. Four professionals and two students are working; spending is under $300 and a colleague will get $2,000. The final report is due at the end of 1960; a 'situational variables' proposal is still pending.

nodes.title: Letter, 2 October 1959
nodes.summary: The researcher thanks the writer for his 29 September letter and the enclosed check, deposited with a redacted body. Work has started, and he hopes to report progress within a few months.

nodes.title: Letter, 25 September 1959
nodes.summary: The researcher is pleased his proposal to survey literature on bioelectric phenomena is approved and accepts the financial terms. A redacted person asked him to keep quiet about a new seismic analyzer backed by major oil companies. He asks the recipient, bound for Europe, to gather names, reports and leading authorities, and for a $400-$500 advance.

nodes.title: Letter, 21 September 1959
nodes.summary: The writer has permission to use administrative funds up to $3,500 for the literature survey, held and paid against vouchers to avoid corporate formality. A redacted person's analyzer seems the most advanced for behavioral science. He plans a trip abroad from 4 to 31 October.

nodes.title: Letter on a new seismic analyzer, September 1959
nodes.summary: Answering a 14 September letter, the writer reports a redacted organization built a new seismic analyzer that handles auto and cross correlation and power spectra on 32 channels at once and may be used for tape-recorded EEG records. An internationally known cardiologist may also support the research. Two copies.

nodes.title: Letter, 14 September 1959
nodes.summary: Short note regretting a missed meeting on Monday night; the letter arrived and suits the writer's purposes.

nodes.title: Memorandum enclosing a pending proposal
nodes.summary: Note enclosing a copy of a proposal pending with a redacted body and mentioning an invitation to meet on 17 September.

nodes.title: Proposal letter, 10 September 1959
nodes.summary: After a visit, the researcher proposes a critical review of literature on recording and interpreting bioelectric signals and activating human behavior by remote means, with three colleagues working unpaid. Five areas; a report within 12 months on $3,500: $1,000 for a typist, $600 consultation, $500 travel, the rest for library services.

nodes.title: Research proposal, 1 July 1959
nodes.summary: A researcher with nine years in electroencephalography proposes a multi-channel electronic analyzer for brain signals, standard variables, clinical diagnostic studies and psychophysiology research. He asks for technical help designing an eight-channel EEG analyzer and about $10,000 in equipment, tied to a new doctoral psychology program.

nodes.title: Letter, 17 August 1959
nodes.summary: Letter arranging a visit for a Thursday night and asking for a hotel reservation.

nodes.title: Letter, 10 August 1959
nodes.summary: The writer would be happy to process a research proposal that falls within his Board of Directors' interests; few grants exceed $15,000, but budget need not limit the plan at first. He plans to stop by on 19 or 20 August.

nodes.title: Letter, 22 July 1959
nodes.summary: A redacted person is out of town until the end of July; the letter is being held for him.

nodes.title: Letter on a situational variables study, 14 July 1959
nodes.summary: Thanking the recipient for a June 1959 report, a researcher asks about a grant to study stimulus situations in human behavior: a taxonomy of situational variables, life space and immediate task, cluster and factor analysis, and four group settings including the military. He asks whether about $15,000 is feasible.
